correctedState: Confirmed, with two wording tightenings. Accurate as claimed: `memory: user|project|local` is parsed and strictly validated in three places (definitions.ts:366-370 plus a throw on an invalid value; pi-harness/runtime-agent-definition.ts:336-339 and :616-620), carried on AgentDefinition (definitions.ts:95) and on the runtime descriptor (:141), spread through to the orchestrator (pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/runtime-agent-definitions.ts:173) - and consumed by nothing. No agent-memory/<name>/ directory is created under any name, in source or in the shipped dist bundles; no MEMORY.md is read on account of the field; Read/Write/Edit are not force-enabled; spawner.ts contains zero occurrences of `memory`. Tightening 1: the fork is not memory-less. A subagent DOES inherit the session/user/project MEMORY.md records as pinned context (capabilities/native-sources.ts discovery -> pi-harness/child-session-port.ts:188 -> context-resource.ts:66), so the missing piece is specifically the PER-AGENT, cross-session-learning store, not memory in general. Tightening 2: 'gets none' overstates the harm slightly - the host never tells the agent it has a private memory directory, so the field is silently inert rather than actively misleading; an author who writes `memory: project` gets strict validation, a value that round-trips, and no per-agent cross-session learning of any kind.
